property_summary: After any successful first Put by an address, the reference contract always allows that same address to perform a subsequent Put (calls do not permanently lock the contract); the mutant that leaves locked_ true causes subsequent Put calls to revert for some inputs.

For any caller and any nonzero payable amount, calling Put twice in a row (with the same caller) on the correct contract always succeeds for the second call (no persistent lock), but the mutant that fails to reset locked_ will make the second Put revert for some inputs (the property checks that the second Put does not revert).

For any caller address and any nonzero ether amount, a second sequential Put(...) call (from the same caller) on the reference C always succeeds (i.e. does not revert) regardless of the first call's parameters; the mutant that leaves locked_ permanently true can make that second Put revert for some inputs.

For any caller and payable amount, performing Put via an external contract whose fallback reverts yields the reference C returning a successful Put (call does not permanently lock when the callee reverts on logging), whereas the mutant that fails to reset locked_ can leave the contract locked and make a subsequent Put call from the same caller fail; the test asserts that two sequential Put attempts (first possibly interacting with a reverting external logger) both succeed on the reference for all admissible inputs but the mutant fails for some inputs.

For any caller and any nonzero payable amount, calling Put once (which invokes Log.AddMessage) never permanently prevents subsequent Put calls from a different caller — i.e., after a successful Put by caller A, a subsequent Put by a different caller B always succeeds on the reference; the mutant that leaves locked_ true can cause that second Put by B to revert for some inputs.

For any caller and any deposit value and unlockTime, the reference contract ensures that after Put(...) the caller's stored unlockTime is at least the current block.timestamp (i.e. acc.unlockTime >= block.timestamp), whereas the mutant allows acc.unlockTime < block.timestamp for some inputs and thus can violate this rule.

For any caller and any inputs, after calling Put(...) the reference C ensures the caller's stored unlockTime is never in the past (acc.unlockTime >= block.timestamp); the mutant sets acc.unlockTime = _unlockTime unconditionally and therefore can make acc.unlockTime < block.timestamp for some inputs, violating this rule.

For any caller and any inputs, after calling Put(...) the reference contract ensures the stored unlockTime for that caller is never decreased below its previous value (acc.unlockTime_new >= acc.unlockTime_old), while the mutant can set acc.unlockTime unconditionally allowing it to decrease for some inputs and thus violate monotonicity.

For any caller and inputs, after calling Put(...) the reference C ensures the caller's stored unlockTime is at least block.timestamp (never in the past); the mutant sets acc.unlockTime = _unlockTime unconditionally, so for some _unlockTime < block.timestamp the stored unlockTime becomes < block.timestamp, violating the rule.

After any Put(...) call, the correct contract guarantees the caller's stored unlockTime is never decreased below its previous value (acc.unlockTime_new >= acc.unlockTime_old); the mutant assigning acc.unlockTime = _unlockTime can reduce unlockTime for some inputs, violating monotonicity.
After a successful Collect call the caller's stored Acc.balance decreases by the withdrawn amount (i.e., new balance = old balance - _am).

property_summary: When the caller's recorded balance is at least MinSum, at least the requested amount, and the unlock time has passed, Collect must not revert (original uses call which may succeed even if contract lacks enough ETH to transfer, while the mutant uses transfer which reverts on failure).

For any caller and amount satisfying the checks, the reference contract always completes Collect(...) (i.e., the external send to msg.sender may fail but is unchecked so the call returns true/false and the contract still updates state only on success), whereas replacing the low-level call with transfer causes Collect(...) to revert when the recipient's fallback reverts or uses more than 2300 gas — so there exist inputs (a malicious/ reverting recipient and an amount) that make the mutated contract revert while the reference would not.

For any caller and amount where the caller has deposited at least MinSum and unlocked funds, calling Collect(...) on the reference always returns (does not revert) — because it uses a low-level call whose failure is handled — whereas the mutant using transfer will revert if the recipient's fallback reverts or consumes too much gas, so some adversarial recipient + amount makes the mutant revert while the reference still succeeds.

For any depositor and amount meeting the withdrawal requirements, the reference contract's Collect(...) call always returns (does not revert) while the mutant using transfer can revert when the recipient's fallback reverts; thus: for every admissible fuzzed depositor and amount, calling Collect(...) on the reference completes (ok == true), but the mutant can make it fail for some inputs involving a reverting recipient.

For any depositor and withdrawal amount where the depositor has deposited >= MinSum and unlocked funds, calling Collect(...) on the reference C always returns (does not revert); the mutant replacing the unchecked low-level call with transfer can revert when the recipient's fallback reverts, so there exists an adversarial recipient that makes the mutant revert while the reference still succeeds.

For any depositor address and amount where the depositor previously called Put with at least MinSum and unlocked funds, calling Collect(...) on the reference C always returns (does not revert) even if the recipient reverts in its fallback; replacing the unchecked low-level call with transfer causes Collect(...) to revert for some malicious recipient fallback, so the reference never reverts while the mutant can.
